assignments.brief_reason: Profanity triggers rejection even if only one side disagrees, fitting high bar removing toxic/vulgar content.
“Not healthy for unbiased public contribution” is a discourse-health criterion not clearly threat/toxicity or violence exception.
Removing offensiveness based on moral compass aligns with removing toxic/offensive content, though threats are not mentioned.
Targets generic name-calling/trolling (“shit-talking”) for removal while keeping constructive speech.
Audience negative reaction is mentioned, but the rationale isn’t clearly mapped to threats/toxicity or violence rules.
Fact-checking and respectful debate are discussed, but it’s unclear this is specifically framed as toxicity/threat moderation.
Uses affect toward right-wing content (“dumb”) rather than explicit toxicity/threat or violence criteria.
Focuses on polarization and whether differences are clearly factual, not directly on threat/toxicity removal rules.
Tone and perceived correctness drive influence, but it doesn’t clearly specify removal criteria for threats/toxicity/violence.
Impartial balancing is described, but not explicitly that identical moderation standards are applied across sides.
Credits language as the main driver without specifying the standard relates to toxicity/threats/violence.
Explicit rules: remove for blatant misinformation and content that could invite violence, while permitting opinions for free speech.
Respect both sides while rejecting personal attacks matches applying consistent standards across political viewpoints.
Direct insult-free threshold: won’t accept content with insults while accepting respectful writing.
States identical standards applied to both sides, focused on harassment/slurs and similar criteria.
Cues center on slurs/demeaning labels and harassment/harm, fitting removing toxic/harassing content.
Evaluates intent/venting and whether respect was given; aligns more with removing disrespectful/toxic behavior than violence exceptions.
Compromise/compassion framing is a general reconciliation perspective without clear moderation thresholds.
Increased perspective taking/opening mind describes an internal effect, not specific moderation rules.
Vague resonance-based comparison process is described without mapping to the codebook’s specific moderation categories.
